Predictions from total-plus-allocation models

Source: R/countreg_alloc.R
predict.countreg_alloc.Rd

Predictions from total-plus-allocation models

Usage

# S3 method for class 'countreg_alloc'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("counts", "prob", "total", "total_positive"),
  conditional = FALSE,
  random = c("marginal", "posterior"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a countreg_alloc() fit.

newdata

optional new data; the estimation data by default.

type

"counts" (default): the expected count in each category, \(E[c]\,\pi_j\); "prob": the allocation probabilities \(\pi_j\); "total": the expected total \(E[c]\); "total_positive": the expected total given at least one event, \(E[c] / (1 - P(0))\).

conditional

for type = "counts": TRUE gives the expected counts given at least one event, \(E[c \mid c > 0]\,\pi_j\). The default is FALSE, the unconditional expected counts, also for a fit with truncated = TRUE (whose estimated distribution is that of the untruncated total).

random

for fits with random parameters: "marginal" (default) averages over the distribution of the random parameters (the prediction for a new unit); "posterior" averages over each unit's posterior distribution given its counts in the estimation data (Empirical Bayes; units not in the estimation data get the marginal prediction). newdata then needs the group_var column(s). The shared site-year term (shared_formula) is always averaged over its distribution, as it is new for every row.

...

unused.

Value

A matrix with one column per category ("counts", "prob"), or a vector ("total", "total_positive"). With random parameters, "prob" is the average allocation probability and "counts" the average expected count over the draws.
